Supply policy your house rules · saved on this device

Perforation margin: refer when the conservative (P90) time-to-perforation is under this multiple of the design life (1.5 = perforation predicted within 1.5× the design life). Perforation within the design life always declines regardless.

House field-calibration your coupon data · saved on this device

Set once from your coupon programme: factor = mean( measured first-year loss ÷ model first-year rate ) across your sites. 1.00 = none (generic ISO). Applied as the default to every assessment and remembered on this device; a per-project coupon above overrides it for that site.

Developer overrides manual model parameters · developer build

Tick a box to replace the auto-derived value with your own; leave unticked to use the model. Yield strength & notes are recorded only — the ISO 9223/9224 corrosion model does not use them.
Adjustment factors applied on top of the values above.
Galvanizers Association Zinc Millennium Map (Annual Average Atmospheric Corrosion of Zinc, UK & Ireland 1998–2000; 10 km ADAS grid). Auto matches your pinned location dynamically: it computes the zinc rate from the live-fetched climate (the map is SO₂-driven, and the tool fetches current CAMS SO₂) and snaps it to the GA 5-category scale — so it tracks the map pin and uses current data (the published grid is 25+ yr old and rates have since fallen). Cat 1–5 = look your site up on the GA map and force that category. Either overrides the site corrosivity (galvanised uses the zinc rate; COR-TEN/carbon use a rate derived via ISO 9223 zinc→category→steel). The GA grid itself is proprietary ADAS data (no public API), so Auto uses the computed equivalent, not a direct grid read. For the finest estimate leave this off (full ISO 9223 from fetched climate).
When on, and the fastener is set to dissimilar and the surface is wet or chloride-loaded, estimates the local galvanic acceleration at the contact (chloride-driven ×2–6, indicative — strongly area-ratio & geometry dependent). Default off = the qualitative bimetallic risk row only.
First-year scales/sets rcorr (the year-1 loss anchor). Projection sets the loss at the design-life year — b is re-derived so the power curve still passes through year-1 and your target. ×multiplier acts on the model value; = sets an absolute value. (Projection factor does not apply to galvanised.)
Service-life planning wrapper: ESL = RSL × A × C × F × G. RSL = the physics reference service life (P90 time-to-perforation from ISO 9223/9224). Only the factors NOT already in the corrosion model are exposed; B, D and E are locked at 1.0 — design/shelter, indoor and outdoor environment are already captured by the exposure class and ISO 9223 corrosivity, and ISO 15686-8 Annex E warns against double-counting. Prefer values 0.8–1.2. Estimate only — not a warranty basis (Annex E).
Override the engine's internal ISO / ASTM constants.
Corrosivity term lifts b from a₀ (benign site) toward the ceiling as the site rate r rises; composition term lowers b by up to cCap for high-alloy grades. Defaults now field-fitted to TRRL LR857 Fig 2a (6 open-exposure COR-TEN B sites): b ≈ 0.10 + 0.0084·r (a₀ 0.10, rDiv 77, floor 0.43, ceiling 0.75) — the open-exposure exponent rises with corrosivity from ~0.44 (rural) to ~0.69 (industrial), corr 0.965. Sheltered surfaces get an additional uplift (below).
Legacy composition-only exponent: b = clamp(a − s·index, floor, ceiling); does not respond to site corrosivity. The set applied depends on the exponent basis above. ISO basis = the original Appendix A.6 formula (unchanged); UK basis = a separate UK-shifted set (COR-TEN B ≈ 0.577 per TRRL).

Least-squares-fitted to TRRL RR233 Table 4 (McKenzie — COR-TEN B / A588 field data only). The measured long-term exponent b is governed by exposure (rain-washed vs sheltered/unwashed), not by corrosivity magnitude — the most corrosive site (Seabegs Open, r≈50 µm/yr) had the lowest exponent (0.577), while lower-rate sheltered sites sat at 0.68–0.74. So b = boldly-exposed value on washed surfaces, sheltered value on sheltered/fascia surfaces; site rate r does not enter. Composition is anchored on the tested grade COR-TEN B (G101 idx 6.39, nudge 0); COR-TEN A is extrapolated via −cS·(idx−6.39) (papers report B corroding faster than A → A slightly lower b). Fit RMSE ≈ 0.018 vs 0.040 for the corrosivity-ride model, and unbiased. Marine / C5–CX / permanently-wet still fail to the residual-benefit model above. Uses the same 3-state Exposure input; the sheltered value is intrinsic (no separate uplift). When this model is active, COR-TEN B is auto-matched to the tested specimen composition (LR857 Table 1: Cu 0.31, Ni nil, Cr 0.57, Si 0.28, P 0.025 → G101 6.39), so the anchor nudge is 0 for the grade the data was measured on.
LR857 Fig 2a — 6 open-exposure COR-TEN B sites (5-yr, this session's digitisation). The open-exposure exponent rises strongly with corrosivity (fitted corr 0.965, range 0.43 rural → 0.72 industrial): b_open = lLo + lSl·(first-year rate µm/yr), clamped 0.43–0.75; sheltered adds lSh (0.13). The shelter uplift is now cross-validated against LR857 Fig 8a girder-sheltered COR-TEN B (6 sites: uplift ≈0.10) + RR233 fascia data (≈0.14) — confirming a positive, corrosivity-independent shelter term. Digitised off the scanned figures (±~0.05); open relation calibrated over rate ≈40–70 µm/yr, extrapolates outside. In this mode the two b values above are ignored. This is the field evidence that site corrosivity — not exposure alone — drives b.
Kihira durable-state model — H. Kihira et al., Corrosion Science 47 (2005) 2377–2390; Nippon Steel Tech. Report 87 (2003). The method behind the Japanese Specification for Highway Bridges (semi-eternal service life). Penetration Y = A·tB (constant B). A_SMA = first-year loss of JIS-SMA weathering steel = the environment's "partial severity" — here taken as the tool's ISO 9223 carbon first-year rate (SMA yr-1 ≈ plain-carbon yr-1). B_SMA(A_SMA) from the paper's Appendix A band (V-shaped, min ≈0.5 at A≈0.03 mm). The alloy conversion A/A_SMA (Eq 3) and B/B_SMA (Eq 4) come from Miki et al.'s empirical V-index (Eq 2) — so BOTH the first-year rate and the exponent respond to composition (Cu/Ni/P/Si + C/Mn/S; no Cr term in Miki's V). Calibrated to Japanese under-girder (sheltered) exposure → conservative vs the boldly-exposed ISO/TRRL bases; the tool's sheltered uplift is therefore suppressed for this model. Verified against the paper's worked point (V=1.538 → A/A_SMA 0.580, B/B_SMA 0.847). The three fields below fill the cert elements absent from the MTC panel (Mo, Ti taken as 0 for COR-TEN); leave at defaults for a typical weathering-steel cast.
Kihira Eq 5 regional-corrosiveness index Z = a·TOW·exp(−j·W)·(C+d·S)/(1+e·C·S)·exp(−Ea/RT) → Eq 6 ASMA = 0.10517·Z + 0.008672 mm (horizontal set-up). Reads the fetched TOW, temperature, chloride Sd→C and SO₂ Pd→S (converted to mg/dm²·d). a=10⁶, d=0.05, Ea=50 kJ/mol are the paper's published constants; j (wind) and e (salt·SO₂ inhibition) are NOT published by Kihira — the defaults below are reasoned estimates, Node-tuned to reproduce the paper's own Chiba worked example (ASMA≈0.049 mm → >1 mm/100 yr). Experimental — calibrate to your data. Wind is used by this route only.
Kihira Section 5: a supplemental treatment is quantified by a P-function — it lowers both the first-year loss (A/A_bare) and the exponent (B/B_bare) because the primer facilitates protective-rust formation — and a T-function X_T — a delay (yr) during which the top coat degrades before rusting starts (Y = 0 until X_T, then the treated power law). Defaults are the paper's Sagamihara 20-yr trial (Ito et al.): A/A_bare 0.316, B/B_bare 0.747, X_T ≈ 3 yr for the primer and ≈ 20 yr with a resin top coat. Kihira flags these vary by environment & treatment and need more data — enter your own product/system values.
When the patina cannot stabilise the loss is ~LINEAR (no self-limiting), per TRRL RR233 (sheltered/marine COR-TEN B showed no decay with time): b = clamp(c₀ − min(mS·(index − p₀), mC), floor, c₀), default c₀≈0.95 (mild-steel-like) with a small alloy edge so COR-TEN A/B stay just below mild. Conservative, field-based (TRRL LR857/RR233).
Long-term exponent basis
UK/TRRL: carbon 0.65→1.0, COR-TEN 0.55–0.74 (boldly→sheltered), failed ~linear — UK-field, ABOVE ISO nominal, more conservative. ISO 9224 nominal: carbon b=0.523, COR-TEN capped ≤0.523, no sheltered uplift — traceable to the standard (note: ISO 9224 publishes no weathering-steel exponent, so COR-TEN < carbon is a bounded in-house choice). The fields below apply in UK mode; galv substrate stays 0.523 in both.
Instead of the patina flipping to failed at a single Sd limit, the ISO 9224 exponent is blended continuously from the stabilised-patina value to the near-carbon value across a chloride band. Removes the step-jump at the gate (and the map-pin jumpiness near the coast). C5/CX corrosivity or a permanently-wet surface still force full reversion. Also smooths the plain-carbon exponent's harsh-gate step (UK basis).
rcorr = a₁·Pd^p₁·exp(c₁·RH + fSt) + a₂·Sd^p₂·exp(c₂·RH + c_T·T),   where fSt = (T≤10 ? f_lo : f_hi)·(T−10)

Data sources
• Climate — temp, RH, time-of-wetness, rainfall: Open-Meteo ERA5 reanalysis (archive-api.open-meteo.com), rolling mean of the last 3 or 5 complete years (selectable; auto-updates).
• Air quality — SO₂: Open-Meteo Air Quality / Copernicus CAMS (air-quality-api.open-meteo.com).
• Location — UK postcode → coords: postcodes.io; place names: Open-Meteo Geocoding.
• Distance-to-coast → chloride: offline UK & Ireland coastline embedded from Natural Earth 10 m — no live call.
• Corrosion model: ISO 9223 / 9224, ASTM G101 / A606, EN 10025-5.
